examples.en: The staff parking lot is behind the school.
The faculty and staff prepared an event for the students.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 교직원만 이용할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only school staff can use this restaurant.
The staff meeting is every Monday.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 교직원 열 명이 새로 왔어요.
examples.en: Ten new staff members arrived for the new semester.
If you ask the staff, they will tell you in detail.

explain: '교사'는 가르치는 사람이고 '교직원'은 교사와 행정 직원까지 학교에서 일하는 사람 전체예요. 대학에서는 '교수'와 '직원'을 합쳐서 '교직원'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The staff cafeteria is on the third floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 일하는 사람들이 쓰는 식당이에요. 학교 안내문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cafeteria for people who work at the school. Often seen in school notices.

phrases.en: There is a staff meeting this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교사와 직원이 모두 모이는 회의를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A meeting that both teachers and office staff attend.

phrases.en: Faculty, staff, and students, please use this door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교 사람들을 모두 말할 때 '학생'과 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 학생 to mean everyone at a school.

explain_en: 교사 means a teacher, while 교직원 covers everyone working at a school, including teachers and administrative staff. At a university it combines 교수 and 직원.

examples.en: My new workplace is close to home, which is nice.
Please write your workplace address on the form.

examples.ko: 근무처가 바뀌면 회사에 바로 알려야 해요.
examples.en: If your workplace changes, you must tell the company right away.

examples.ko: 근무처에서 오는 전화는 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: I have to take calls that come from my workplace.

examples.ko: 지금 근무처까지 지하철로 사십 분 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes forty minutes by subway to my current workplace.
Since I changed workplaces, I work fewer late nights.

explain: '직장'이 일하는 곳을 두루 말한다면 '근무처'는 서류의 칸 이름이나 연락처를 쓸 때 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '회사', '직장'이라고 말해요.

phrases.en: Please write your workplace phone number on the form too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류의 칸 이름으로 자주 보는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common label on forms.

phrases.en: I'm changing my workplace next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 회사 안에서 일하는 곳이 바뀔 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used when the place changes within the same company.

phrases.en: Excuse me, where do you work?
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 정중하게 일하는 곳을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat polite way to ask where someone works.

explain_en: '직장' is the general word for where you work, while '근무처' often appears as a field name on forms or contact details. In casual talk people usually say '회사' or '직장'.

examples.en: All the staff work wearing name tags.
The name tag has the name and grade written on it.
I got a new name tag for the new semester.
You can't enter without a name badge.
Please sew the name tag onto the uniform.
On the event day, we hang name tags around our necks.

explain: 가슴이나 목에 다는 이름표예요. '이름표'는 더 일상적이고, '명찰'은 회사·학교·군대처럼 공식적인 곳에서 자주 써요. '명찰을 달다/차다/걸다'로 말해요.

phrases.en: Please put a name tag on your chest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명찰'보다 일상적이고 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday, simpler word than 명찰.

phrases.example: 행사 직원은 모두 명찰을 달아야 해요.
phrases.en: All event staff must wear a name tag.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷에 명찰을 붙일 때 가장 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for attaching a name tag to clothing.

phrases.en: Hang your name tag around your neck and go in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목걸이 형태일 때 '걸다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 걸다 when the tag hangs around the neck.

explain_en: It is a name tag worn on the chest or around the neck. '이름표' is more everyday, while '명찰' is used often in formal places like companies, schools and the military. You say '명찰을 달다/차다/걸다'.

examples.ko: 마침 일요일이라 수련의들은 휴일도 반납하고 달려왔어요.
examples.en: It happened to be Sunday, but the interns gave up their day off and rushed in.
Doctors in training learn a lot from senior doctors.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 병원에서 수련의로 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm currently working at the hospital as a resident.
The resident stayed by the patient's side all night.

examples.ko: 수련의 시절에는 잠을 거의 못 잤어요.
examples.en: During my residency, I barely slept.
I asked the resident my questions.

explain: 의사 면허를 딴 뒤 병원에서 전문 과정을 밟는 의사를 말해요. 일상에서는 '인턴', '레지던트'라는 말도 많이 쓰고, 공식적인 이름은 '전공의'예요.

phrases.en: I'm working as an intern at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 막 일을 시작한 수련의를 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual word for a doctor just starting training.

phrases.en: He is a resident in internal medicine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인턴 다음 단계로 전문 과목을 배우는 의사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The stage after intern, training in a specialty.

phrases.en: The residents cared for patients all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적인 이름이라 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The official term, common in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to a licensed doctor undergoing specialist training at a hospital. In daily talk people also say '인턴' and '레지던트', and the official term is '전공의'.

examples.en: The president arrived with a large entourage.
An attendant arrived first and checked the venue.

examples.ko: 그 장관은 수행원 없이 혼자 공항에 나왔어요.
examples.en: That minister came to the airport alone, without an entourage.
I went on the business trip as the boss's attendant.
The attendants manage the schedule so the guest is comfortable.
How many attendants will you be bringing?

explain: 높은 사람을 따라다니며 돕는 사람을 말해요. 연예인을 챙기는 사람은 보통 '매니저'라고 하고, '수행원'은 대통령이나 외국 손님 같은 중요한 사람 이야기에 잘 어울려요. '임무 수행'의 '수행'과는 소리만 같고 한자가 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The prime minister was followed by ten attendants.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 사람이 이동할 때 사람들이 함께 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people accompany an important person when moving.

phrases.en: The entourage entered the hotel.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 다니는 사람들 전체를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the whole group traveling together.

phrases.en: The boss doesn't keep a separate attendant.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 다니며 돕는 사람을 곁에 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to keep a helper who goes along with you.

explain_en: It refers to people who accompany and assist an important person. For someone looking after a celebrity, '매니저' is the usual word, while '수행원' fits stories about presidents or foreign guests. It sounds the same as '수행' in '임무 수행', but the Chinese characters are different.

examples.en: The groom escorted the bride as they entered.
The bodyguard escorted the guest to the car.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 친구를 집 앞까지 에스코트해 줬어요.
examples.en: On a rainy day I escorted my friend to her door.

examples.ko: 남자가 꼭 여자를 에스코트해야 하는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: A man doesn't always have to escort a woman.
A staff member came out to escort us to the meeting room.

examples.ko: 어두운 밤길에서는 서로 에스코트하며 걷기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to walk the dark night road escorting each other.

explain: '바래다주다'가 집까지 데려다주는 일상적인 말이라면, '에스코트하다'는 결혼식, 행사, 경호처럼 예의 있게 곁에서 안내하고 동행하는 느낌이에요. 영어 escort에서 온 말이라 약간 멋을 낸 분위기가 있어요.

phrases.en: A staff member escorted me to the meeting room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가를 예의 있게 안내하고 동행해 줄 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when someone accompanies and guides a person politely.

phrases.example: 신부는 아버지의 에스코트를 받아 걸어 들어왔어요.
phrases.en: The bride walked in escorted by her father.
phrases.nuance_ko: 에스코트를 받는 사람이 주어일 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person being escorted is the subject.

phrases.en: My friend took me home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집까지 데려다주는 일상적인 말이라 '에스코트하다'보다 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday word for seeing someone home; more casual than 에스코트하다.

explain_en: '바래다주다' is the everyday word for seeing someone home, while '에스코트하다' suggests courteously accompanying and guiding someone, as at weddings, events or in security work. It comes from English 'escort' and has a slightly stylish feel.

examples.en: A female flight attendant handed out drinks on the plane.

examples.ko: 여승무원은 안전 교육을 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Female crew members must receive safety training.
My friend passed the exam to become a flight attendant.
The female crew members greeted us with smiles.
I asked the female train attendant for directions.
When I was little, my dream was to be a flight attendant.

explain: 비행기나 열차에서 일하는 여성 승무원을 가리키지만, 성별을 따로 밝힐 필요가 없으면 그냥 '승무원'이라고 해도 돼요. 같은 틀로 '남승무원'도 있어요.

phrases.en: My older sister works as a female flight attendant for an airline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비행기에서 일하는 여성 승무원을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a woman who works aboard an airplane.

phrases.en: There was also a male crew member on this flight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 틀로 만든 말로, 남자 승무원을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Built the same way, referring to a male crew member.

phrases.en: The crew member checked the seat belts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성별을 밝힐 필요가 없을 때 쓰는 더 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more general term when gender doesn't need to be mentioned.

explain_en: It refers to a woman working as crew on a plane or train, but if you don't need to mention gender, simply saying '승무원' is fine. The same pattern gives '남승무원' for men.

examples.en: If you lose your passport, ask the consul for help.
A consul protects citizens of their own country who live abroad.
You have to make a reservation first to meet the consul.

examples.ko: 새로 온 영사가 교민 모임에 참석했어요.
examples.en: The newly arrived consul attended a meeting of overseas Koreans.
I got home safely with the consul's help.

examples.ko: 그 대사관에서 일하는 영사와 인사를 나눴어요.
examples.en: I greeted the consul who works at that embassy.

explain: 대사는 나라를 대표해 정치적인 일을 하고, 영사는 여권이나 비자처럼 국민과 직접 관련된 일을 맡아요. 일하는 곳도 보통 대사는 대사관, 영사는 영사관이에요. 가장 높은 영사는 '총영사'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I went to the consulate and applied for a visa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영사가 일하는 곳으로, 여권이나 비자 일을 하러 갈 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The place where a consul works, often mentioned for passport or visa matters.

phrases.en: The consul general attended the event for overseas Koreans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영사 중에서 가장 높은 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The title for the highest-ranking consul.

phrases.en: Reissuing a passport falls under consular work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에 사는 자국민을 돕는 일을 가리킬 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the work of helping one's citizens who live abroad.

explain_en: An 대사 represents the country and handles political matters, while a 영사 deals with things directly tied to citizens, such as passports and visas. Usually an 대사 works at an 대사관 and a 영사 at an 영사관. The highest-ranking consul is called a 총영사.

examples.en: The teaching assistant handed out the class materials.
If you have a question, ask the teaching assistant.
My older brother works as a teaching assistant in graduate school.
Thanks to the teaching assistant, I finished my homework well.
A teaching assistant helps the professor with work.
They say the lab is hiring a new teaching assistant.

explain: 대학이나 학원에서 교수님이나 강사를 도와주는 사람이에요. 직접 부를 때는 '조교님'이라고 해요. 선생님과 달리 수업을 맡기보다 자료 준비, 채점, 질문 응답을 돕는 보조 역할이 중심이에요.

phrases.en: Teaching assistant, when is this homework due?
phrases.nuance_ko: 조교를 직접 부르거나 말할 때 존경을 담아 붙이는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The respectful form used when addressing or referring to a TA directly.

phrases.en: I work as a teaching assistant at a university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업이나 역할을 말할 때 '~로 일하다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~로 일하다' to talk about a job or role.

phrases.en: The class TA helps with grading.
phrases.nuance_ko: 특정 수업을 돕는 조교를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a TA who assists with a specific class.

explain_en: A person who assists the professor or instructor at a university or academy. You address them as '조교님'. Unlike a teacher, they mostly support with materials, grading, and answering questions rather than leading the class.

examples.en: The principal will retire at the end of this year.
The president stepped down after working for a long time.
The president left office and returned to the hometown.
On the day of the retirement, the staff gave a bouquet.

examples.ko: 그 의사는 병원에서 퇴임한 후에도 봉사를 해요.
examples.en: That doctor still volunteers after leaving the hospital post.

examples.ko: 내년에 퇴임할 예정이라서 요즘 정리하고 있어요.
examples.en: I plan to step down next year, so I am sorting things out these days.

explain: 일반 직원이 회사를 그만둘 때는 '퇴직하다'나 '그만두다'를 쓰고, '퇴임하다'는 사장, 교장, 대통령처럼 맡은 자리에서 물러날 때 써요. 반대말은 '취임하다'예요. 정년이 되어 일을 마치는 건 '정년퇴직하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Tomorrow is the principal's retirement ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에서 물러날 때 하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the ceremony held when someone leaves a post.

phrases.en: After retiring, I want to live in my hometown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리에서 물러난 뒤의 시간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time after leaving a post.

phrases.en: The president is going to retire next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 물러날 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a planned future retirement.

explain_en: For ordinary employees leaving a company, use 퇴직하다 or 그만두다. 퇴임하다 is for stepping down from a post held by someone like a president, principal or head of state. The opposite is 취임하다. Finishing work at retirement age is 정년퇴직하다.

examples.en: The editorial department reread the article and fixed it.
I work in the editorial department of a magazine company.

examples.ko: 편집부 직원들이 마감 때문에 밤을 새웠어요.
examples.en: The editorial staff stayed up all night because of the deadline.
You can send the manuscript to the editorial department.
A newspaper's editorial department also decides the headlines.

examples.ko: 편집부 회의가 오후 세 시에 열려요.
examples.en: The editorial meeting is held at three in the afternoon.

explain: 편집부는 신문사, 출판사, 잡지사에서 글을 고치고 지면을 짜는 부서예요. 취재하는 곳은 '취재부', 광고를 파는 곳은 '광고부'처럼 부서 이름에 '부'를 붙여요. 한 사람은 '편집자'나 '에디터'라고 불러요.

phrases.example: 편집부 직원이 제 글을 읽어 줬어요.
phrases.en: An editorial department staff member read my writing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서에서 일하는 사람을 말할 때 뒤에 '직원'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 직원 to refer to someone working in the department.

phrases.en: There is an editorial department meeting this afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부서 안에서 하는 회의를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a meeting held within the department.

phrases.en: I'm an editor who makes books.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편집부'는 부서이고, '편집자'는 그곳에서 일하는 한 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 편집부 is the department, while 편집자 is one person who works there.

explain_en: 편집부 is the department at a newspaper, publisher or magazine that edits text and lays out pages. Department names take 부, as in 취재부 (reporting) and 광고부 (advertising). One person there is a 편집자 or an 에디터.

en: dean (of a college within a university)

examples.en: The dean of our college is very kind.
The dean gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation ceremony.
A new person has come as dean of the art college.
I asked the dean about scholarships.
I made an appointment for a meeting with the dean.

examples.ko: 그분은 학장이 되기 전에 오랫동안 교수였어요.
examples.en: Before becoming dean, that person was a professor for many years.

explain: '총장'은 대학 전체의 우두머리이고, '학장'은 공과대학·인문대학 같은 단과대학의 우두머리예요. 직접 부를 때는 '학장님'이라고 해요. 고등학교의 우두머리는 '학장'이 아니라 '교장'이에요.

phrases.en: I greeted the dean.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직접 부르거나 높여 말할 때는 '님'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 님 when addressing or referring to the dean respectfully.

phrases.en: I had a meeting in the dean's office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학장이 일하는 방을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the room where the dean works.

phrases.en: A new dean of the engineering college has arrived.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 단과대학인지 앞에 붙여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the name of the college in front to say which one.

explain_en: A 총장 heads the whole university, while a 학장 heads one college inside it, such as engineering or humanities. When addressing the person directly, say 학장님. The head of a high school is a 교장, not a 학장.
